title: Put a pea-sized dab of toothpaste on a child's toothbrush: squeeze 0.15-0.35 g from a kids' tube onto the bristles
instruction: Get the toothbrush ready for a 4-year-old.
context: Children aged 3 to 6 should brush with no more than a pea-sized amount of fluoride toothpaste (about 0.25 g; a smear the size of a grain of rice under age 3), as the CDC, ADA and AAP advise, yet over 38% of US children aged 3 to 6 use more (CDC MMWR 2019;68(4):87-90), which raises the risk of dental fluorosis. Parents dose a brush twice a day. One hand holds the brush bristles-up while the other squeezes: the dose is set by how far and how long the tube is squeezed, and a yield-stress paste keeps coming briefly after the squeeze stops, so too much is the easy failure.
setup: Positions are in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, with x forward, y to the robot's left and the counter (table) top at z 0. Toothbrush: a child's manual toothbrush for ages 3-5 (e.g. Colgate Kids extra soft), about 15.1 cm long, 14 g: a 95 x 16 x 12 mm handle, a 30 mm neck and a 26 x 12 mm head carrying a 20 x 9 mm bristle field 9 mm tall (measure the trial brush). It lies on its back, bristles up, along x with the head away from the robot, the bristle field's top middle at (32.0, 8.0, 1.4). Toothpaste: a Crest Kid's Cavity Protection 4.2 oz (119 g) laminate tube, half used (60 g of paste left, 1.30 g/mL), flip cap open: a round body 34 mm across and 10 cm long, a flat crimped end 46 mm wide, a 30 mm flip cap with a 5 mm nozzle; 15.0 cm overall as modeled (measure the trial tube). It lies on its side along x, nozzle toward the robot, its body's middle at (25.0, -15.0, 1.7). Both arms start at their ready pose.
scoring: Paste on the bristles is weighed: grams = mL x 1.30 g/mL. 0.75: 0.15 to 0.35 g on the bristle field (a pea-sized dab, 0.25 g, the dose for ages 3-6) and at most 0.05 g anywhere else (counter, head sides, neck, handle). 0.5: a pea-sized dab but more than 0.05 g off the bristles. 0.25: 0.05 to 0.15 g (a smear or rice grain, the under-3 dose) or 0.35 to 0.70 g (too much, a half load). 0: under 0.05 g or over 0.70 g (a full adult strip). 1.0: the 0.75 state with the bristles within 45 degrees of facing up (held or set down) and the tube lying on the counter, released, both still for 1 s. Turning the bristles past sideways with paste on them caps the score at 0.25 (the dab can fall or smear). Doing nothing scores 0. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0. In simulation paste lands on the bristles only while they face within 60 degrees of up. Real trial: weigh the brush and the tube on a 0.01 g scale before; after, photograph the head from above against a mm scale, wipe any paste off the brush outside the bristle field with a tissue and weigh the brush (paste on the bristles); weigh the tube unwiped (paste dispensed); off the bristles = dispensed minus on the bristles. Bristle angle and tube release from the video. Each weight is independent of where the brush ends up.
reset_notes: Each trial uses a clean, dry brush (weighed) laid at its mark, and the tube at its mark with 50 to 70 g of paste left (gross weight minus 12 g): roll it flat from the crimp up to the paste, wipe the nozzle flush, cap open, and let it lie 1 min so the laminate springs back. Start a new tube by squeezing 59 g into a cup. In simulation the tube always holds 60 g and the brush starts clean.
fidelity: Rigid bodies. The tube is a rigid core with four sprung wall panels; the paste is a flow model, not a fluid: pressure from the panels' push on 8 mL of air, a 0.7 kPa yield pressure, flow past it, dropped plumb from the nozzle onto a 1 mm grid of the bristle field that moves with the brush and slumps above 4.5 mm. Paste weight, stringing and soaking into bristles are not modeled. The squeeze-to-dose constants are estimates, calibrated on the trial tube (README).
